result.narrative:
Vardhit Auto Components Limited is carrying one open overdue notification under policy TCI-WT-2026-0002, an invoice of INR 7.0m now 36 days past due, against total exposure of INR 26m on an INR 60m limit. That is a clear break from the established pattern: the last four resolved notifications all cleared within 3-6 days of due date over the preceding ~10 months, and the payment trend is marked deteriorating. Notification frequency itself is not accelerating (2 in the last 6 months versus 3 prior), so the concern is severity rather than volume.

The score is 27.3, placing the buyer in Watch, from 0.65 x 42.0 (payment, 36 DPD) + 0.35 x 0.0 (news) = 27.3, with a PD of 0.173. The entire score is driven by that single notification; the news screen returned severity 0 with no article, no headline and no parent linkage, and both the news and parent evidence queries came back empty. The adjudicator agreed with caveats and flagged three issues worth resolving before acting: the notification is dated 2026-10-18 while citing an original due date of 2026-10-18 yet is scored at 36 DPD, which cannot both be true; the structured record shows owed 26,000,000 INR while the narrative describes INR 7.0m actually past due against INR 26m exposure, so the 'owed' field appears to hold total exposure; and all notifications come from one policy with one insurer, so there is no cross-carrier validation and no resolution date for the open item.

The recommendation is MAINTAIN on the single limit: TCI, insured Orvana Steel, whole turnover, current limit INR 60,000,000 held unchanged, because probability of default of 0.173 is within the 0.25 appetite target and maximum liability does not bind. Expected loss is 7,473,600 both before and after. No reduction is proposed at this score, but the deterioration is real and the adjudicator's caveats mean the underwriter should confirm the 36 DPD figure and the true past-due amount against the source ledger, and confirm the news screen actually ran, before treating the Watch band as settled.

What would lift this is straightforward: settlement of the open INR 7.0m invoice and a return to the prior 3-6 day clearance pattern. The score sits 7.3 points above the Healthy line at 20.0, so a resolved overdue with lower DPD moves the buyer down a band. Conversely the buyer is 22.7 points below the High Risk threshold of 50.0, which would be reached at 54 DPD on the current payment-only profile.

judgement.bottom_line: Maintain the INR 60,000,000 TCI limit — PD of 0.173 is within the 0.25 appetite target — but note the adjudicator agreed only with caveats: the sole scored notification carries an internal date contradiction (dated 2026-10-18 with an original due date of 2026-10-18 yet scored 36 DPD) and an amount inconsistency (INR 7.0m past due versus an 'owed' field of 26,000,000), both of which should be confirmed against the source ledger.
judgement.payment_note: One open overdue of INR 7.0m at 36 days past due against INR 26m exposure, a deteriorating trend and a sharp break from the last four resolved notifications, which all cleared within 3-6 days of due date.
judgement.news_note: No matched news — the screen returned severity 0 with no article, headline or parent linkage, and the news and parent evidence queries were both empty, so this is an absence of evidence rather than a confirmed clean record.

Score falling 7.3 points to below 20.0 reaches Healthy
Ledger confirmation that the 36 DPD figure is overstated, given the 2026-10-18 date contradiction
